answer: Admission PoW at the saffron gate: each identity must burn a unique puzzle averaging 500 CPU-hours, so 1,000 sybils cost ~500,000 CPU-hours (~$12 each on spot instances, ~$12k total). The walnut commits the nonce to the applicant's key, blocking replay or shared work. The beacon chain timestamps each solution, so a farm cannot precompute ahead or reuse proofs. Cost scales linearly with identities while rewards stay flat, driving operator return negative past a handful. This works because forgery expense exceeds any sybil payoff.
